content: Digoxin is a medication that may interact with other drugs and supplements. Before starting digoxin, inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and other supplements you are taking. This will help your provider assess potential interactions. For more details, refer to the interactions section below. Pregnancy: It is not clear whether digoxin can affect pregnancy or harm an unborn baby. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider. They will determine whether you should continue taking digoxin during pregnancy or while trying to conceive. Breastfeeding: Digoxin is known to pass into breast milk. If you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, notify your healthcare provider to discuss the potential risks and benefits. Drug Interactions with Foods and Drinks: The absorption of oral digoxin may be reduced if taken with meals high in bran fiber. It is unclear whether alcohol consumption affects digoxin directly. However, drinking alcohol while on digoxin may increase the risk of side effects such as dizziness, blurred vision, and confusion. Drug Interactions with Other Medications: Digoxin can interact with many other medications. Always inform your healthcare provider about all drugs you are taking to avoid harmful interactions. Overdose: If you or someone else has taken too much digoxin, stop using the medication immediately and seek medical attention. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose of digoxin, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses to make up for the missed one. How to Use: Digoxin is available as a liquid or tablet to be swallowed, or as a liquid for injection into a blood vessel or muscle. Follow your healthcare provider’s instructions for proper use. Common Side Effects: The most common side effects of digoxin include: Heart problems, such as changes in heart rate or rhythm. Loss of appetite. Nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Stomach pain or intestinal issues. Blurred vision or seeing yellow/green halos. Headache. Weakness. Dizziness. Confusion. Anxiety, depression, or hallucinations. Enlarged breasts in men. Rash. If any of these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. There may be other side effects not listed here. Contact your provider if you suspect you are experiencing a side effect. Serious Side Effects: Less common but serious side effects include: Severe allergic reactions, such as difficulty breathing, wheezing, rapid heartbeat, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, throat tightness, itching, rash, or hives. Heart rate or rhythm changes, such as bradycardia (slow heart rate), irregular heartbeat, or fainting. In rare cases, this can lead to cardiac arrest. People with pre-existing heart disease or those taking other heart-affecting medications are at higher risk. If you experience chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting, confusion, or extreme fatigue, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Digoxin Toxicity: Excessive levels of digoxin in the body can lead to toxicity. Symptoms of digoxin toxicity include: Loss of appetite. Nausea or vomiting. Persistent diarrhea. Confusion. Weakness. Vision changes. Abnormal heart rhythms (arrhythmias), including fast or slow heartbeats. If you suspect digoxin toxicity, stop taking the medication and contact your healthcare provider immediately. Additional medical tests may be required to confirm the diagnosis. Precautions: Who Should Not Use Digoxin: Individuals allergic to digoxin, digitalis, Lanoxin, or any ingredients in the specific product should not take this medication. Your pharmacist can provide a list of ingredients in the digoxin product you are prescribed. People with ventricular fibrillation, a type of abnormal heart rhythm, should not use digoxin. Important Considerations Before Use: Do not take digoxin unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. Take it exactly as directed. Do not share digoxin with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. Keep digoxin out of reach of children. Digoxin may affect alertness or coordination. Avoid driving or performing activities requiring alertness until you know how the medication affects you. Digoxin can influence blood pressure and heart rate. Discuss with your provider how to monitor these symptoms. If prescribed digoxin oral solution, use the oral syringe provided to measure your dose accurately. Consult your pharmacist if you are unsure how to measure your dose. Medical History: Inform your healthcare provider if you have any of the following conditions: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. Sinus node disease or sick sinus syndrome. Atrioventricular (AV) block. Kidney problems. Myocarditis (inflammation of the heart muscle). Heart failure with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. Thyroid problems. Chronic diarrhea. Electrolyte Imbalances: Notify your provider if you have a history of electrolyte imbalances, such as: Low potassium levels (hypokalemia). Low magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia). Low calcium levels (hypocalcemia). High calcium levels (hypercalcemia). Medical Procedures: If you are undergoing a procedure called electrical cardioversion, inform your provider that you are taking digoxin. Other Medications and Supplements: Digoxin may interact with other medications and supplements. Always inform your provider about all prescription and over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: The effects of digoxin on pregnancy and unborn babies are unknown. Inform your provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Digoxin passes into breast milk. Notify your provider if you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed.
